title: Exponential family as a Wikipedia density class
dek: Encyclopedia class: T(y) and A(η). The GLM hook and TB-lab examples already live on stats-exponential-family.
story: Exponential family on Wikipedia is a density class whose log is linear in a finite sufficient statistic. Bernoulli, Poisson, Gaussian-with-known-variance, gamma, multinomial sit inside (or in a dispersion extension).
stats-exponential-family already does mean = A', variance = A'', and the GLM hook. This card is the encyclopedia class name and the graph of cousins (quasi-likelihood, mixtures that leave the class).
NIST remains definitional authority if a talk page fights about the 'regular' versus 'curved' exponential family. Curved families (e.g. some N(θ,θ²) stories) are a footnote, not a TB DST likelihood.
deep: Finite T(y) is the punchline: if your model needs the whole residual list as sufficient, you left.
Mixtures and random effects generally leave the one-parameter exponential family in the mixing weight.
Canonical links exist because η is the natural parameter.
Do not call a Cox partial likelihood a full exponential-family density without extra care.

visual.caption: Class members and the exit door. Size is TB-notebook frequency, matching the existing expfam plate's teaching weights without copying its prose.
